name: Nia Chen
role: peer-generation caster; first network contact for the party; the Act I→II hinge NPC
disposition: slightly-older-sibling; casual competence; easy laugh; does not perform authority
description: Early 30s, Taiwanese-American, born in San Jose, lives in a small Mission apartment with a roommate who is never home. Practical urban clothes — worn Blundstones, a good-enough coat, a canvas tote she's had since college. Wears her hair short and slightly uneven, as if she cut it herself in front of a bathroom mirror on a Tuesday and it worked. Has the settled body language of someone who has done what the PCs are starting.
voice: Casual, mid-range Bay-Area English; quick to laugh; interrupts herself with follow-ups; uses your first name warmly on the second beat of every conversation. Does NOT sound like a mentor. Sounds like an older cousin who has been through it and is glad to see you.
signature: The venue signature: never meets the party in a private home; always in a peer-adult-urban spot — a WeWork lobby coffee bar, a boba shop, a Muni platform.
The network-shape line: 'We don't have a guild hall. We have lunch in twos.'

The authorless-cause line, delivered when a PC asks who saved them: 'People ask me who saved them. I used to think it was us — reaching out without knowing. Now I think the world just doesn't permit the version where you weren't here. We didn't do it. Nothing did. I can't tell you what. Neither can anyone.'

The Reggie-naming, if a PC brings up someone weird at SFO or a person who seems to feel things: 'Oh — is that Reggie? He's one of us in a way. Feels the pattern; won't ever cast. He'll always know when a caster is in the room. It's a lonely position; kindness helps.'
The gentle refusal of the mentor frame: 'I'm not going to teach you. I'm going to have lunch with you. Different thing.'
dmNotes:
**RENAME NOTE — critical.** This NPC was named 'Mira Chen' throughout the design docs (big-arc.md, hook-ledger.md, facts-ledger.md, various episode files). She has been renamed to **Nia Chen** because the original name collides with the PC **Mira Sun** (Slot 3). All future references in DM docs should use 'Nia Chen.' Legacy 'Mira Chen' references in design/DM-ONLY/*.md and episode files remain textually until swept, but the NPC's canonical name going forward is Nia.

**The Act I→II hinge NPC** (per big-arc.md §Act I Hook to Act II + hook A1). Nia is the character who introduces the caster network and names its unknowability. She is NOT the Wise Old Sage; she is the slightly-older sibling who has done what the PCs are starting. Big-arc canon: she introduces the network *and* names the unknowability — she cannot give them a culprit, because there isn't one.

**Voice discipline: CASUAL-COMPETENT.** Nia is not Vivian's-unhurried-dying, not Bea's-dry-amused, not Rosa's-sharp-kind, not Alaia's-reserved-watchful. Nia is *casual*. She laughs. She interrupts herself. She uses your first name early. She has the settled body language of a person who has been through the arc the PCs are entering — she remembers her own Phase 1 and Phase 2, and she is glad the PCs have made it this far. She does not perform authority; she does not perform mystery. She is a peer-cohort adult with a job and a roommate and a bike, who happens to be a caster.

**Venue discipline — critical.** Per Expert 3 variety-audit finding (from campaign design review): the party has already had elder-in-home scenes with Bea (Outer Sunset), Vivian (Sacramento suburb), and will have another with Rosa (Berkeley Hills). Nia's introduction MUST use a **peer-adult-urban setting** to break the pattern. Recommended venues:
- A **WeWork lobby coffee bar** in SoMa (Nia works freelance and uses one; she'll wave the party over between meetings).
- A **boba shop** near her apartment in the Mission (she has an order they know).
- A **Muni platform** at Powell or 16th & Mission (an ambient-city meet — she was passing through; can walk with the party as they talk).
- A **park bench** at Dolores or Mission Dolores steps (a Sunday-morning frame).

Do NOT meet Nia at a private home. Do NOT meet Nia at a mentor-coded space (a bookshop back room, a garden, an office). Peer-adult-urban is her frame; it does structural work for the arc's cadence.

**Introduction pathway.** Nia is introduced via **Bea's referral** at the Act I→II hinge (Ep 6-8 target window per hook A1). Independent of Sacramento (Sacramento is the Loewe/Vivian arc-node; Nia comes through the Bay Area network via Bea, not via Dakota's thread). Bea's referral shape (a note, a phone number written on the back of an index card, a text to a number Bea rarely uses): *'Nia will meet you. Don't push. Let her ask what she wants to know.'* Bea will not explain further.

**The two invariant lines Nia delivers.** These are load-bearing arc payoff — deliver both, ideally in the same scene:
1. **Network shape:** *'We don't have a guild hall. We have lunch in twos.'*
2. **Authorless cause:** *'People ask me who saved them. I used to think it was us — reaching out without knowing. Now I think the world just doesn't permit the version where you weren't here. We didn't do it. Nothing did. I can't tell you what. Neither can anyone.'*

Big-arc calls out these as the load-bearing arc-payoff lines that resolve the Ep 1 gate mystery permanently-open. Do not paraphrase; deliver as close to verbatim as the scene allows.

**Reggie's substrate-sensitivity named** (hook A2).

> [!CAUTION]
> **A2 MOVED TO EP 9 (2026-08-30) — and this beat is PLAYER-TRIGGERED, which is the problem.** If a player raises Reggie at the Ep 8 lunch — likely, since he is a played NPC and Nia is the first network caster they have met — she cannot simply refuse to answer; that is out of character for someone casual and quick to follow up.
>
> **Her Ep 8 deflection, which is honest and costs nothing:** *"Oh — yeah, I've heard about people like that. Not my area. Ask me when I've had more coffee."* Interested, unbothered, and moving on. **She is not hiding anything; it genuinely is not her subject.**
>
> **If a player pushes twice, let A2 fire in Ep 8 rather than have her stonewall.** A stonewalling Nia costs more than an early A2. Log it and drop A2 from Ep 9.

 If the PCs bring up someone weird at SFO or a person who seems to feel patterns without being able to act on them, Nia references Reggie by name — she has met him once, or knows of him through the network's ambient awareness of substrate-sensitive non-casters in the Bay Area. Her line names him as an example of the network-adjacent non-caster archetype. This retroactively explains his Ep 3 face-changed-twice reaction. Deliver as casual observation, not revelation.

**The unfamiliar-clustering structural rule** (per big-arc.md §Act I Hook to Act II). Nia tells the PCs the network is structurally diffuse: *clustering unfamiliar casters creates social pressure that breaks intent integrity.* The five-person party is exempt — they have already come to know each other's shape and their cohesion is stable (they paid the cost across Eps 1-N). Where the friction bites is when the party brings *multiple* network casters into a single meeting, or tries to assemble a council. This is the invariant that keeps the arc from turning into a wizard-council story. Deliver as practical advice: *'Don't try to meet more than two of us at a time. It stops working when there are too many of us in a room. I don't know why — nobody does — it just does.'*

**THE PARTY'S OWN COHESION — corrected 2026-08-30 (facts-ledger §45).** An earlier version had her close that line with *'You five are fine, obviously; you've had time.'* **Cut it.** It is an NPC explaining why the party works, which is the one thing no NPC may do — see the Eps 6-8 standing negative duty. Her replacement, said as a shrug and never defended:

> *'You five seem to be fine. I don't know why. Time, maybe.'*

**She offers it as a guess and drops it.** If a player pushes, she is genuinely uninterested — *'that's the part I don't have an explanation for'* — and changes the subject. **Familiarity remains the real mechanism for the network at large (invariant 5 is untouched); what she must not do is close the question about THESE five.** Per §45, the arrow between *how they met* and *their wants don't contest the same ground* is never drawn aloud, by anyone, ever.

**She is peer-generation, not elder.** Early 30s. Has been casting for ~8 years (started in her mid-twenties, went through her own Phase 1 and Phase 2 alone; Phase 3 release came at 29 in a moment of unforced calm on a bike ride in Golden Gate Park). She is NOT the party's mentor; she is the party's slightly-older peer who is willing to have lunch with them. She has her own life — she is a UX-research contractor freelancing between tech and nonprofit clients; she has a therapist; she has a Peloton she doesn't use; she has a running text-thread with two other network peers whose names she will not share with the party.

**What she knows (delivers as arc-appropriate):**
- The network's shape (lunch-in-twos; magic-punishes-grouping).
- The authorless-cause frame (permanent unknowability of who saved whom).
- Reggie's substrate-sensitivity (A2 payoff).
- The existence of other casters (she will not name them; if the party pushes, she says 'When they find you, they'll find you').
- Her own cast domain (DM's soft call: **timing** — Nia casts small nudges in *when* things happen; a bus arrives at the right moment, a text comes at the right minute. Peripheral to arc; texture only).
- The network's factional stances at a high level (Hidden vs Selective per big-arc). She herself leans **Selective** — she believes magic should be selectively revealed to those who can hold it, which is why she is willing to meet the PCs now that Bea has vouched. She does not lecture them about this; she embodies it.

**What she does NOT know:**
- The Loewe/Annex 7 thread (that is the older-generation Vega/Vivian arc; not Nia's inheritance).
- The excised-pages diagram (facts-ledger §21).
- Companion or the AI arc (that is Act II-III institutional discovery; not yet in her frame).
- The word 'substrate' (she uses 'the pattern,' 'the reaching,' 'the shape').

**Cross-references:** hook A1 (Nia introduced as network contact — the Act I→II hinge), hook A2 (Reggie substrate-sensitivity named), hook B3 (network faction alignment choice — Nia is Selective-leaning), Ep 1 gate mystery permanent-open (authorless-cause line resolves the frame). Big-arc.md §Act I Hook to Act II (canonical). Facts-ledger §9 (Reggie substrate-sensitivity), §2 (ledger-network hint — Nia may say 'we don't have a guild hall; we have ledgers' as an alternate framing).

**Never voice at the table:** any explicit substrate vocabulary; any Act II-III institutional detail (Companion, the Founder trinity); any specific naming of other network casters beyond Reggie (who is not a caster) and Rosa (whom the party will already know by the time Nia lands). Nia's role is the *hinge*; she opens the door but does not walk the party through the next rooms.

**Risk if unresolved:** A1 is the load-bearing Act I→II hinge. Without Nia, the party has been introduced to the pattern but has no peer-cohort proof of the network. The arc stalls at 'we know weird things happen' rather than progressing to 'we are one node in a diffuse group.' Bake the Nia introduction into Ep 6-8; do not defer past Ep 8.

background.homeBase: A small two-bedroom Mission apartment; roommate is a flight attendant who is rarely home
background.household: Roommate (traveling most of the time); no partner currently; a small planter of herbs on the fire escape that survives despite her neglect
background.family: Parents in San Jose (retired engineers). Younger brother in Seattle (product manager). Family knows nothing about the network — she has never told them; she is not sure they would understand, and she is not interested in finding out this year
background.career: UX-research contractor freelancing between mid-size tech clients and civil-society nonprofits. Comfortable-not-wealthy; picks up work she cares about; turns down work she doesn't. Formal training: HCI master's at Cal ~8 years ago. That period is when she first cast
background.hobbies: Rides a bike everywhere. Reads mostly nonfiction; occasionally poetry when she needs to. Has a bad Peloton habit of buying subscriptions and not using them. Runs a small text-thread with two other network peers whose names she will not share
